threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, key deliverables and roles for the tax workflow project.

messages.text:
Kicking off the Standardised Corporate Tax Filing Workflow Rollout for this channel.
Scope as I understand it: map our current end-to-end process, define a standard workflow and RACI, and get it in place before the next monthly filing cycle.
Key deliverables from the project brief include the process map and RACI, review and sign-off procedure, and the training pack. A1 and T1 plus T5 look like the backbone for the workflow and responsibilities.
Proposal on roles:
- Tax clerks: own process mapping, checklist, review/sign-off procedure
- Secretary: own calendar, shared folders, training pack and pilot coordination
Can you all confirm if this matches expectations, and which filing cycles and client segments we should include in the first rollout?

Thanks for starting this.
On scope: I agree that A1 plus T1 and T5 should anchor the workflow. From an audit perspective, we should also make sure the workflow covers how we evidence checks and approvals.
For the first rollout, I suggest we focus on:
- Monthly VAT and payroll filings
- Corporate income tax prepayments where due next month
Client segments: small and mid-size corporate clients only, excluding complex groups and cross-border cases for the first cycle.
Happy to co-own the process map and RACI with you and validate that the review steps are robust enough.

I am aligned with the scope and the split between tax clerks and secretary.
On filing cycles, focusing on monthly VAT and payroll makes sense to me. For client segments, could we also include a small sample of the more complex clients, maybe just one or two, so that T1 captures their specific steps and we do not miss key variations in A1?

I can help document the current steps for the smaller clients for T1.
One question: when we say end-to-end, do we include how we receive documents from clients and how we archive them, or is that part of another task? I want to be sure I capture the right start and end points in the process map.

Good question. For T1, I suggest we map from initial data request to final submission and immediate archiving.
The detailed retention rules will sit in a separate guideline, but the process map in A1 should still show where documents are stored and who is responsible.
So for your part of T1, please include:
- How we request and receive data
- Where we store working files
- How we confirm submission and archive evidence.

From the secretary side, I can take T3, T6, T7 and T10.
For the first rollout, I will set up the calendar only for:
- Monthly VAT
- Monthly payroll
- Any corporate income tax prepayments due in the next 30 days
I will also prepare a simple overview slide for the workflow once A1 and T5 are stable, and then we can add it into the training pack.

On including complex clients in the first rollout: I would keep the workflow design generic enough to handle them, but for the initial implementation I would limit the live use to small and mid-size clients.
However, for T1 we can still map one or two complex cases as examples, clearly flagged as advanced variations in A1. That way we do not delay the rollout but still capture the extra steps.
Understood. I can take one complex client and document the extra steps as a variation for T1, clearly marked as such, so it feeds into A1 without being part of the first live cycle.

On ownership of deliverables, here is a concrete proposal:
- A1 (Standard Tax Filing Workflow and RACI): owned by 48446, with 104021 as co-reviewer
- T1 (current process map): split between 315923 for small clients and 390807 for complex variations, consolidated by me
- T5 (quality review and sign-off procedure): drafted by 104021, with my support
- Secretary-owned items: T3, T6, T7, T10 as proposed by 497040
If there are no objections, we can treat this as the working allocation for D1.

The ownership proposal works for me.
For T5, I will draft the review and sign-off procedure so that it aligns with audit expectations and then we can integrate it into A1 and the checklist later.

I am ok to take the small client mapping for T1.
I will start with the last two months of VAT and payroll filings and write down the steps we actually followed, then share a draft for review.

I confirm I will take T3, T6, T7 and T10.
I will need guidance on which client list to use for the first calendar and pilot, so once D2 is confirmed, I will set those up.

To close D2, let me summarise what I am hearing:
- Filing cycles in scope for first rollout: monthly VAT, monthly payroll, and any corporate income tax prepayments due in the next monthly cycle
- Client segments: small and mid-size corporate clients for live use; one or two complex clients documented only as process variations in T1 and A1, not part of the first live cycle
Unless anyone disagrees today, we will treat this as the agreed scope for the first rollout.

The summary for D2 matches my understanding.
This scope should be manageable before the next monthly cycle and still give us enough coverage to test the workflow.

Agreed on the scope for D2.
I will pick one complex client for documentation only and make sure it is clearly labelled as a variation in T1.

Quick recap for this thread:
- D1: ownership of A1, T1, T5 and secretary tasks confirmed as per M9
- D2: first rollout scope confirmed as per M13
Next, we should move into detailed mapping for T1 and drafting T5 so that A1 can be assembled in time for the next cycle.

threads.thread_goal: Design and iterate on the tax return preparation checklist and review steps.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the Tax Return Preparation and Review Checklist for T2, which will become A2.
Structure so far:
1) Pre-filing data collection
2) Calculations and reconciliations
3) Review and sign-off
4) Filing and archiving
I have also added a section for common error checks based on our experience, but I have not yet linked it to the top recurring errors from T8 or to A7.
Please review the structure and suggest any missing mandatory items, especially around fraud red-flag checks and documentation of review steps.

Thanks for sharing the draft.
From a tax legislation and bookkeeping perspective, I would suggest we explicitly separate:
- Data completeness checks (all required ledgers, bank statements, payroll reports)
- Tax rule application checks (rates, exemptions, thresholds)
- Cross-checks against prior periods and financial statements
For fraud red flags, A7 from T8 should drive a dedicated subsection in A2, not just scattered items. Maybe a short list of must-do checks per filing type.
I also recommend we embed the sign-off steps from T5 directly into the review section so that A2 and A5 are consistent.

I like the four-part structure.
One thing I often miss in practice is a clear step to confirm that the client has approved the draft figures before we file. Could we add a mandatory item in the review section to record client confirmation (email or signed summary) and where it is stored, so it ties back to the documentation guideline later?

I have a question on how detailed the checklist should be.
For example, for VAT, do we list each specific report we need to extract from the accounting system, or do we keep it more generic like 'obtain VAT ledger and supporting documents'? I want to avoid making A2 too long to use, but also not miss anything important.

Good point. My suggestion is:
- Keep A2 at the level of mandatory categories (for example, VAT ledger, bank statements, sales and purchase listings)
- Where needed, we can add a short note or link to a separate how-to for system-specific steps, so the checklist remains usable across clients.
For fraud checks, we should be more explicit. A7 from T8 will give us the top recurring issues, and we can translate those into concrete yes or no checks in A2.

Agree on client approval.
I would add under the review section:
- Prepare a short summary of key figures and changes vs prior period
- Send to client for confirmation
- Record confirmation and store it in the client folder as per the retention guideline
This will also align with A4 later.
We should mark this as mandatory for all corporate income tax and for VAT where there are material changes.

I will rework the draft of A2 to:
- Split the checks into completeness, tax rule application, and cross-checks
- Add a dedicated fraud red-flag section driven by A7
- Integrate the sign-off steps from T5, including thresholds for second-level review
Once done, I will share a second draft and we can see if it is ready for pilot use under T2.

Understood.
Once the next draft is ready, I can test A2 on a recent VAT filing and note where I get stuck or where steps feel unclear. That might help refine the wording for people who are newer to the process.

When you add the fraud red-flag section, could we group the checks by filing type (VAT, payroll, corporate income tax) and mark which ones are mandatory vs optional? That would make it easier to apply in practice.
We should also make sure that any red flag automatically triggers a note in the working papers, so that if there is a later query we can show what we did.

Yes, grouping by filing type and marking mandatory checks makes sense.
I will also add a field in A2 to record any red flags identified and how they were resolved, which will tie into the documentation and query handling guidelines later.

To move towards D3, here is a proposed final structure for A2:
1) Pre-filing data collection (by filing type)
2) Completeness checks
3) Tax rule application checks
4) Cross-checks vs financial statements and prior periods
5) Fraud red-flag checks (grouped by filing type, mandatory items clearly marked)
6) Review and sign-off (including thresholds from T5 and client approval)
7) Filing and archiving
If everyone is comfortable with this structure, we can treat it as the agreed backbone for the checklist and focus further comments on wording and examples.

I agree with the proposed structure for D3.
For D4, I would summarise the fraud integration as:
- Dedicated section in A2 with mandatory checks per filing type
- Clear instruction that any red flag must be documented and, where needed, escalated according to the review procedure in T5
- Link to A7 for background and examples, but keep the operational checks inside A2.
If there are no objections, we can consider this the agreed approach for fraud checks.

I am aligned with both D3 and D4 as summarised.
Once the updated A2 is ready, I can run it on one payroll and one VAT filing and capture any practical issues before we roll it out more widely under T2.

The structure looks clear to me and I like that the fraud checks are grouped and marked as mandatory.
I will pay attention to how easy it is to follow in practice when I test it on a recent filing.

Recap for this thread:
- D3: we have agreed the structure and mandatory sections of A2 as per M27
- D4: we have agreed how fraud red-flag checks are integrated into A2 as per M28
Next step is for 104021 to update A2 accordingly and for 315923 and 390807 to pilot it on a few recent filings under T2.

threads.thread_goal: Set up and validate the deadlines calendar and filing status control sheet.

messages.text:
I have created an initial version of the tax deadlines calendar and the filing status control sheet for T3 and T11.
- Calendar (A3): includes monthly VAT and payroll deadlines, plus corporate income tax prepayments due in the next 30 days, segmented by client type (small vs mid-size) and tax authority.
- Control sheet (A6): lists active clients in scope, with columns for filing type, due date, preparer, reviewer, and status (not started / in progress / ready for review / submitted).
Please review and confirm which deadlines and client types must be tracked in A3 for D5, and whether we need any additional fields in A6 for D6.

Thanks for setting this up.
For A3, I would suggest we also include:
- Annual corporate income tax filing deadlines for clients where the due date falls within the next 3 months
- Any known one-off obligations (for example, local business tax) that fall in the same period
This will help us avoid missing less frequent obligations.
For A6, I recommend adding fields for date of review completion and date of submission, so we can evidence timeliness and support any internal audit checks.

On D5, I agree with the focus on monthly VAT, payroll, and upcoming prepayments.
I would add that for any client in the first rollout, all recurring tax obligations that fall within the next monthly cycle should be in A3, even if they are quarterly, as long as the due date is within that window.
On A6 for D6, we should also capture who is responsible for providing source data on the client side, or at least a contact field, so we know whom to chase when we are close to deadlines.

Looking at A6, I think it would help to have a simple risk flag column (for example, high / normal) so we can quickly see which filings need extra attention, such as new clients or those with a history of late submissions.
For A3, could we also add reminder dates for preparation and review, not just the filing deadline, so that we can plan workload better?

I checked the calendar and control sheet.
For A6, I sometimes lose track of which filings are waiting for client documents. Maybe we could add a simple field like 'waiting for client' yes or no, so we can see where we are blocked.

I can extend A3 to include:
- Annual corporate income tax deadlines within the next 3 months
- One-off obligations that fall in that period
I will also add reminder events for preparation and review, for example, 10 days before and 5 days before the filing deadline, as suggested.

For A6, I will add the following fields:
- Client contact name or email
- Date review completed
- Date submitted
- Risk flag
- Waiting for client (yes or no)
Once updated, I will share a new version for validation under T11.

To make D5 explicit, I propose we define the scope of A3 as:
- All monthly VAT and payroll filings for small and mid-size corporate clients in the first rollout
- Any quarterly or annual obligations for those clients where the due date falls within the next 3 months
- Any corporate income tax prepayments due in the same period
Plus reminder events for preparation and review.
If everyone agrees, we can treat this as the final list of deadlines and client types to track for D5.

I agree with the scope for D5 as you summarised it.
This should give us enough coverage without overloading the calendar.

Aligned on D5.
Once the updated A3 is ready, I can cross-check a sample of clients against our existing deadlines list to make sure nothing obvious is missing.

For D6, I suggest we define the minimum required fields in A6 as:
- Client name
- Filing type
- Tax authority
- Due date
- Preparer
- Reviewer
- Status
- Date review completed
- Date submitted
- Waiting for client (yes or no)
Optional but recommended: client contact and risk flag.
If we agree on this, we can lock D6 and then refine layout and filters later.

The list of fields for D6 works for me.
The 'waiting for client' field will be especially helpful to see where we are blocked.

Agreed on D6.
These fields should be enough to manage the workflow and support any internal audit sampling.

Thanks for the feedback.
I will update A3 and A6 according to the agreed scope for D5 and the minimum fields for D6, then share links in the channel once done so we can start using them in the next cycle under T3 and T11.

threads.thread_goal: Close on documentation, retention and query handling guidelines.

messages.text:
I have drafted initial versions of the documentation and evidence retention guideline (T4 leading to A4) and the quality review and sign-off procedure (T5 leading to A5). 104021 has also started outlining the procedure for handling tax authority queries under T9, which will become A8.
Key points in A4:
- Retention periods by document type (working papers, client source documents, submissions, correspondence)
- Storage locations and naming conventions
- Confidentiality and access rules
For A8:
- Steps for logging and assessing queries
- Response timelines and escalation rules
- Template responses
Please review and share any concerns, especially around retention periods and how A8 should link back to A2 and A5.

Adding some detail from the query handling side.
In A8, I have structured the process as:
1) Receive and log query (including deadline and reference number)
2) Retrieve relevant working papers and submissions from A4 locations
3) Analyse and draft response
4) Internal review and sign-off (aligned with A5)
5) Send response and archive correspondence
6) Capture any lessons learned and update A2 or A4 if needed
I would like feedback on whether the retention periods in A4 are sufficient to cover typical audit and dispute windows, and whether we need any extra steps for sensitive cases.

On A4, I think it would help to have a simple table that shows for each document type: minimum retention period, storage folder, and who can access it.
For example, working papers vs client source documents might have different access rules.
Also, should we have a clear rule on when to anonymise or redact documents if we use them for training or examples?

I have a question on retention periods.
If a client leaves us, do we keep their documents for the same period as active clients, or do we shorten it? I want to be sure I do not delete anything too early.

For retention, we should base the periods on tax legislation and typical audit windows, not on whether the client is active.
So even if a client leaves, we keep their records for the same minimum period. After that, we can delete or archive according to our general policy.
I will make this explicit in A4 so there is no confusion.

Good idea on the table.
I will help refine A4 so that for each document type we specify:
- Retention period
- Storage location
- Access level (for example, all tax clerks vs restricted to senior staff)
On anonymisation, I agree we should state that any documents used for training must be anonymised or redacted, and that we should never share client-identifiable data outside the restricted folders.

On A8, could we add a simple priority classification for queries (for example, urgent, normal) based on the response deadline from the tax authority?
Also, it might help to have a field to record whether the query relates to a known red flag from A7, so we can track patterns and update A2 or A4 accordingly.

For retention periods in A4, my proposal is:
- Working papers and submissions: at least 10 years
- Client source documents: at least 10 years, unless legislation requires longer
- Correspondence with tax authorities: at least 10 years from closure of the matter
This should cover typical audit and dispute windows in our jurisdiction.
If we agree, we can lock these as the standard periods for D7, with a note that any stricter legal requirement overrides them.

I support the proposed retention periods for D7.
We should also add a short note in A4 that any ongoing dispute or investigation automatically extends the retention period until the matter is fully closed.

The 10-year rule is clear and easy to remember.
The note about ongoing disputes will also help me know when not to delete anything.

For D8, I suggest we define the standard procedure in A8 as follows:
- All tax authority queries are logged with deadline, reference, and priority
- Relevant working papers and submissions are retrieved from locations defined in A4
- Draft responses are prepared by the responsible tax clerk and reviewed according to A5 (including second-level review where thresholds are met)
- Responses are sent before the deadline and all correspondence is archived under the client folder
- Any recurring themes or links to known red flags from A7 are captured and used to update A2 and A4 under T12.
If there are no objections, we can treat this as the approved standard for D8.

I am aligned with D8 as summarised.
The link back to A2 and A4 via T12 will help us keep the workflow up to date when we see new patterns in queries.

To close this thread:
- D7: we have agreed on standard retention periods and storage rules in A4 as per M53, with clarifications from M54
- D8: we have agreed on the standard procedure for handling tax authority queries in A8 as per M56
Next steps are to finalise A4, A5 and A8 under T4, T5, T9 and T12, and then share them for a short sign-off by the tax compliance manager role.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot run of the new workflow on selected clients.

messages.text:
Time to plan the pilot run of the new workflow before the next monthly cycle.
Based on A1, A2, A3 and A6, I propose the following for T10:
- Pilot scope: 5 small and 3 mid-size corporate clients, covering VAT, payroll, and any prepayments due next month
- Timeline: start preparation 10 days before deadlines, with review checkpoints 5 days before
I will coordinate calendar invites and a short feedback form as part of T7.
Please suggest which specific clients we should include and how you want to collect and act on feedback for D9 and D10.

For the pilot client list, I suggest we choose:
- 3 small clients with straightforward VAT and payroll
- 2 small clients with known recurring issues (for example, late documents)
- 3 mid-size clients with higher transaction volumes
This will give us a mix of simple and slightly more challenging cases.
On feedback, I recommend we use a short form plus a quick debrief call after the cycle to capture what worked and what did not, and then map any changes back to A1, A2, A3, A4 and A6.

I agree with the mix proposed by 104021.
For D9, I suggest we finalise the list as:
- Small straightforward: Clients S1, S2, S3
- Small with recurring issues: Clients S4, S5
- Mid-size: Clients M1, M2, M3
We should avoid including any very complex group structures in this first pilot.
On timeline, starting preparation 10 days before and review 5 days before is realistic if we stick to the new checklist A2 and use A6 to track status.

I can take responsibility for two of the mid-size clients in the pilot.
For feedback, it would help if the form asks specifically about:
- Clarity of A2
- Usefulness of A3 reminders
- How easy it was to keep A6 up to date
So we can see which parts of the workflow need the most adjustment.

I am happy to handle one or two of the small straightforward clients in the pilot.
It would be useful if the training pack under T7 includes a one-page example of a fully completed A2 and A6 entry, so I can check if I am using them correctly.

I will set up T10 using the client list you proposed:
- S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, M1, M2, M3
I will add them to A3 with specific pilot tags and create entries in A6 so we can track them separately.
For the timeline, I will send calendar invites for preparation and review checkpoints 10 and 5 days before each deadline.

To make D9 explicit, we can state:
- Pilot clients: S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, M1, M2, M3
- Pilot timeline: next monthly cycle, with preparation starting 10 days before deadlines and review 5 days before
If everyone agrees, we can treat this as the final decision for D9.

Agreed on D9.
This set of clients should give us a good spread of scenarios without overloading the team.

For D10, I propose the following feedback approach:
- Short online form after each filing, with questions on A1, A2, A3, A4 and A6
- One debrief call at the end of the cycle to discuss themes and agree changes
I can draft the form as part of T7 and share it here for comments before we start the pilot.

The feedback approach works for me.
It would be helpful if the form also has a free-text field for any unexpected issues, so we do not miss things that do not fit the predefined questions.

I support the combination of form plus debrief call for D10.
We should also agree that any changes to A1, A2, A3, A4 or A6 coming out of the pilot will be logged under T12 so that we keep a clear history of updates.

To formalise D10, I suggest we state:
- Feedback will be collected via a short form after each pilot filing, plus one end-of-cycle debrief call
- The form will cover clarity and usability of A1, A2, A3, A4 and A6, and include a free-text field for other issues
- Any agreed changes will be implemented under T12 and reflected in the relevant artifacts.
If there are no objections, we can treat this as the agreed approach for D10.

I am fine with D10.
The form plus call will give me a chance to raise any points I might forget during the cycle.

Recap for this thread:
- D9: pilot clients and timeline confirmed as per M65
- D10: feedback collection and follow-up approach confirmed as per M70
Next steps for me under T6, T7 and T10 are to finalise the shared folder structure, prepare the training and feedback form, and schedule the pilot checkpoints in A3 and A6.
